headline: Reliance lifts Sensex 1,233 points, FM open to capital gains tax review

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Tuesday, the third of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, Reliance Industries carried the market. Its shares jumped 11.6 percent after record quarterly profit, their biggest one-day rise in over six years, and the Sensex closed up 1,233 points.

Second, the tax on long-term capital gains is back in play. The market regulator has recommended scrapping it for foreign investors, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said she will consider the call for a review, because, in her words, the voices of concern are louder.

Third, a busy day ahead. State Bank of India reports results today, and Americans vote in the midterm elections, while oil has dropped sharply on hopes of peace talks with Iran.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
On Monday, the Sensex rose 1,233 points and the Nifty gained 388 points, a jump of nearly 2 percent, with the Nifty reclaiming the 23,400 mark. Falling crude oil, strong results and foreign buying set the mood. Reliance alone added about 1.83 lakh crore rupees to its market value. Metals and cement stocks also gained.

Now to the flows. Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth about 3,115 crore rupees, their second straight day of buying. Domestic institutions sold about 392 crore rupees. But the longer trend is stark. The Economic Times says foreign holding has hit multi-year lows in about 70 percent of India's top 100 companies, and Mint finds foreign investors cut their stake in 57 of 100 large companies in the September quarter.

In the bond market, the ten-year government bond yield fell nearly 10 basis points to 7.32 percent as crude slid.

The levels to watch. Analysts put immediate resistance for the Nifty at 23,500, then 23,600, where a gap from the ninth of September remains open, and then 23,800 to 24,000. Support sits at 23,200 to 23,300. GIFT Nifty was around 23,550 early this morning, pointing to a firm start.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
To new listings. EAAA India Alternatives listed at a small premium and closed 3.77 percent above its issue price, at 1,727 rupees 80 paise. On debut day, HDFC Mutual Fund, Carnelian Asset Management and L and T together picked up about 2.9 percent of the company in bulk deals worth about 316 crore rupees.

In the pipeline, Coal India has filed draft papers to list its subsidiary South Eastern Coalfields, selling 66.81 crore shares, or 10 percent of the company. And StockGro, an investing app with over 35 million users, has filed for an IPO after tripling its profit to about 113 crore rupees last financial year.

The bigger picture: a Grant Thornton Bharat report says main-board IPOs raised a record 84,400 crore rupees in the first half of this financial year, up 30 percent, from 71 companies. Average listing-day gains rose to 18 percent. But Mint notes foreign investors' share of IPO anchor books has fallen to a five-year low, with domestic institutions stepping in.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results. Motilal Oswal says this has been the strongest quarter of profit growth in 12 quarters, and it has raised its earnings estimates for the Nifty.

In consumer goods, ITC's consolidated profit fell 18.5 percent to 4,229 crore rupees. Higher cigarette taxes hurt, with the company absorbing part of the price increases, and cigarette operating profit fell more than 27 percent. On the other side, its non-cigarette businesses had their best revenue growth in 14 quarters. Marico had a stronger quarter. Profit jumped 31 percent on 13 percent revenue growth, though it flagged rising input costs from the West Asia conflict and poor weather.

In finance, Fusion Finance swung to a profit of 86.5 crore rupees from a loss a year ago, with bad loans down to 1.6 percent. In pharma, Granules India reported a 39 percent jump in profit. Container Corporation's profit dipped slightly.

Today's big one is State Bank of India. Analysts expect net interest income to grow 11 to 13 percent, though they differ on profit. NSE, Bajaj Finserv, Solar Industries and Lloyds Metals also report.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
To the economy, and the tax debate first. The market regulator has proposed scrapping the 12.5 percent long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors, and tax relief for mutual fund investors who switch schemes. SBI Research goes further. It suggests no tax on gains held over three years, a 2 lakh rupee exemption, and a 50 percent rise in securities transaction tax, putting the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees. Jefferies says a cut could ease foreign outflows and support the rupee. But Bernstein's Venugopal Garre says a cut alone would not bring sustained foreign inflows. The finance minister also said the government will keep up its capital spending push, guided by fiscal prudence.

That prudence will be tested. SBI Research estimates the central fiscal deficit could overshoot the budget target by about 1.2 lakh crore rupees this year, on higher fertiliser, cooking gas and fuel subsidies. Ahead of next year's budget, the government is also reviewing customs duty concessions on 118 goods that are due to expire.

On the data, the HSBC manufacturing purchasing managers' index eased to 54.7 in October from 55.1, but export orders grew at their fastest pace in six months, and selling price inflation was the lowest in nearly four years. Car sales hit a record, and daily UPI payments touched 1 lakh crore rupees.

In banking, a month after the Reserve Bank's rate hike, banks have begun raising deposit rates as liquidity tightens. Bank of India is the latest, with a special 500-day deposit.

On trade, India and the European Union discussed customs and implementation ahead of signing their trade deal in December.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, oil is the big mover. Prices fell around 6 to 7 percent on Monday after Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian signalled openness to talks, and officials met Qatari mediators. This morning Brent is steady near 105 dollars a barrel, nudging up after reports of fresh US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, even as President Trump says Iran wants a deal. Gold and silver bounced from multi-month lows as the oil slide eased inflation worries.

On Wall Street, the rotation out of technology continued. The Nasdaq fell 1.1 percent and the Nasdaq 100 slipped into a correction, while the S and P 500 lost half a percent and the Dow gained 0.4 percent. Marvell dropped 12 percent after announcing a 115 billion dollar deal for Lumentum, and Oracle fell 8 percent on plans to raise capital for its AI build-out. US Treasuries rallied as falling oil eased fears of more Fed rate hikes. Asian markets are mostly lower this morning.

Americans vote in the midterm elections today. Moneycontrol notes Democrats have widened their poll lead, and the prediction market Polymarket gives them about a 95 percent chance of taking the House.

In China, authorities will push financial institutions to make fuller use of two stock support tools. And in crypto, the FBI has blamed North Korea for the 6.3 billion dollar theft from Binance, the biggest crypto heist on record. North Korea denies it.

segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. Parent Reliance surged 11.6 percent on Monday, and Business Standard now values its 64.5 percent stake in Jio Platforms at about 8.37 lakh crore rupees. Motilal Oswal's wealth research desk calls the Jio listing a re-rating catalyst for the whole telecom sector, including Airtel.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now, your money. Fixed deposit rates are inching up after the Reserve Bank's October rate hike, so it's worth checking what your bank now offers.

A few tax points. The return filing deadline for audit cases has been pushed to the twenty-first of November. The Delhi bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted an addition of 1.13 crore rupees after accepting that 3.9 kilos of jewellery found at a man's home belonged to his late wife and three married daughters, a reminder to keep proof of who owns family gold. Got a Diwali gift from your employer? Gifts under 15,000 rupees may be tax-free, but a cash bonus is taxed from the first rupee.

For freelancers and service exporters, the Reserve Bank has simplified export declaration rules under the foreign exchange law, with a 10 lakh rupee threshold and relief for resident individuals.

Gold, before Dhanteras. The evening rate for 24 carat gold fell 2,530 rupees to about 1,37,524 rupees per 10 grams on Monday, and silver slipped below 1.8 lakh rupees a kilo.

One date for your calendar. Coal India, Asian Paints and Godrej Consumer have set tomorrow, the fourth, as the record date for their interim dividends, and Concord Biotech for its one-for-one bonus. Under next-day settlement, shares must be bought by today to qualify.

And some relief for patients. The drug price regulator has cut maximum retail prices on 543 cancer medicines from the ninth of November, which it estimates could save patients 2,500 to 3,500 crore rupees a year. Central government staff also get a 3 percent dearness allowance hike, to 63 percent of basic pay.

That's your brief. Today, watch State Bank of India's results, whether the Nifty can clear 23,500, oil prices as the Iran talks unfold, and the US midterm results overnight. Have a good day.
